sources.title: IT request export (three rows, supplied in chat on 2026-09-21)
sources.summary: TI-31 open in 'Diagnose the problem' since 2026-09-10; TI-32 open in 'Classify the request' since 2026-09-16; TI-29 closed 2026-09-12 after 6 days. No timezone, no observation time, no due dates, no assignees, no workflow version. TI-30 absent.

sections.title: TI-31 open in 'Diagnose the problem' since 2026-09-10
TI-32 open in 'Classify the request' since 2026-09-16

decisions.question: Who owns the IT request process (the person accountable for the change below and for reviewing overdue TI actions)? The export names no owner and no manifest existed.

Proposed change: set a due offset of 1 workday from activation on 'Classify the request' and 3 workdays from activation on 'Diagnose the problem', with the process owner reviewing the overdue list twice a week. Measure in the October 2026 export: median time in each state, share completed within due, count of cases. Accept, adjust the offsets, or reject?
Which group holds 'Classify the request' and which holds 'Diagnose the problem'? The export carries no assignee, so the attention items cannot be routed to a named group.
What happened to TI-30? It is absent from an export that contains TI-29, TI-31 and TI-32 (cancelled, filtered out, or in a state the export omits).

Next month's export must carry: observation date-time and timezone, case id, current action, action activation and completion date-times, due date, assignee group, workflow version, and closed cases with open and close date-times. Confirm who produces it and on which date (proposed: 2026-10-31, Africa/Luanda).

Are the dates in the export in Africa/Luanda? TI-29 closed on a Saturday (2026-09-12) and, if '6 days' is calendar days, opened on a Sunday (2026-09-06). Either weekend work happens or the dates are in another timezone (UTC) or truncated.
